speaker_role: independent college admissions consultant (Julie Kim, Julie Kim Consulting)
commercial_incentive: Repeatedly promotes her paid 'Passion Project Boot Camp' / 'Ideal League Formula' program and a free masterclass at her consulting website.
key_insights: Advises 9th graders to establish a personal 'theme' for their application by the end of freshman year, defined as academic interest plus personal interest plus 'SPV' (strength, personality, values).

Argues elite colleges build a well-rounded class out of specialized students, not well-rounded individuals, so being known for a distinct combination of traits matters more than doing many unrelated activities.

Suggests students can't determine their passions by sitting and thinking; clarity on interests only comes from taking action (trying things), likened to not knowing if you like Thai food without tasting it.
Recommends pursuing 'passion projects' and reaching out to professors as a way to both build application material and genuinely deepen interest/clarity over time.
Claims guiding students to approach professors 'professionally' has helped some land research positions or internships, not because of existing expertise but because of how the outreach is done.
Third checklist item: freshmen should identify their own academic strengths/weaknesses (e.g., fast reader, works better alone vs. in groups) to guide course and study-strategy choices going forward.
notable_or_distinctive: The 'academic interest + personal interest + SPV (strength/personality/values)' theme formula is a distinctive proprietary framework, though presented without evidence it improves outcomes.
reliability_notes: Heavily promotional (masterclass/program plugged twice); claims about theme-building and professor outreach leading to research positions are anecdotal and unsupported by data.
